Hi @jdbway, @kommander — thank you @jdbway for the detailed reproduction steps! Submitted PR #49560 to address this:

1. **Surfacing nested/sibling projects:** The picker now queries `sdk.client.project.list()` globally and merges all registered project worktrees and directories under the "Other" section, so nested projects like `/work/repos/HomeLab` appear and match fuzzy search.
2. **Path prompt on `ctrl+m`:** Pressing `ctrl+m` ("new") now opens `DialogPrompt` to enter an arbitrary target directory path directly, while falling back to git worktree creation if left blank.
3. **Cross-project relocation:** The backend engine now allows moving sessions to arbitrary directories and across distinct projects without raising `DestinationProjectMismatchError`.

Hi @kommander, @timrichardson — thank you @timrichardson for the earlier investigation and proposal in #44829!

Submitted PR #49560 to resolve this for active sessions on the current `dev` branch architecture by updating `useDirectory()` in `packages/tui/src/context/directory.ts` to inspect the active session's directory (`session?.directory`) as soon as `SessionEvent.Moved` is projected.

Seems that something is broken in the Snap version of the OpenCode Desktop app, such that it is reporting the incorrect version number. I was able to run normally in the TUI but the Desktop App kept receiving this error.

I was able to remedy by uninstalling the SNAP version and installing the .deb directly.

Confirming this is still present on **v1.18.31** (latest release, 2026-09-14), on macOS arm64 with `opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0`, opened from another machine as `http://192.168.x.x:4096`.

Repro and evidence from this instance:

- Attach via the "+" button → no chip, no toast, nothing in the console UI; message sends text-only.
- Server DB (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) shows the user messages with `text` parts only, zero `file` parts. Network request to `POST /session/{id}/prompt_async` carries `parts = [{type:"text"}]` only, so the attachment never leaves the browser.
- Bundle inspection of the served `index-*.js` matches the source: `blobID()` (`packages/app/src/utils/draft-store.ts`) calls `crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", ...)` unconditionally, and the hidden `<input type=file>` change handler calls `addAttachments()` without `await`/`.catch`, so the `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'digest')` rejects unhandled — hence the fully silent drop.
- Notably `uuid()` in the same app already guards with `globalThis.isSecureContext`; `blobID()` is the remaining unguarded call site (plus the V2 composer path noted above).

Workaround confirmed working: tunnel the port and use `http://localhost:4096` from the client (`ssh -L 4096:localhost:4096 user@host`), since localhost is a secure context. HTTPS origins work too.
superseded by #48937 and #49126, verified against v2.0.10.

I'm having the same problem (with deepseek) here; it's a pain because the session gets lost since it gets stuck in that infinite error loop.

check: https://github.com/ArminShupuk/compliant-eyeballs

Fixes this exact problem. There are multiple bigger projects with the same issue. There won't be a compliant implementation in Node.js anytime soon due to refactoring issues, so I created this library. Any other solution is either a reinvention of happy eyeballs or a tradeoff between reducing latency failures and increasing overall connection time.

**Atualização: build funcional e descoberta importante sobre cross-compile** ✅

O binário Windows traduzido agora funciona de ponta a ponta (incluindo envio de prompts). Uma descoberta relevante para o upstream:

### ⚠️ `bun run build` no Windows gera binário com bug

Ao buildar o `packages/opencode` **nativamente no Windows**, o binário resultante falha ao enviar qualquer prompt com:
```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')
```
no `LayerNode.walk` (`packages/core/src/effect/layer-node.ts`) — ocorre ao montar o grafo `locationServices` no `SystemPrompt.environment`.

Testei: bun 1.4.2 e 1.3.14, com/sem `--minify`, com/sem web UI embed, config isolada — **todo build no Windows falha**.

### ✅ Cross-compile no Linux resolve

Buildar o **mesmo código** no Linux (WSL/Ubuntu 24.04, como o GitHub Actions faz) gera um binário Windows **funcional**:
```bash
wsl
cd packages/opencode
bun run build   # builda todos os targets, inclui opencode-windows-x64
```
Teste validado: `opencode.exe run "diga OK"` responde corretamente (exit 0).

O release oficial sempre foi cross-compilado no Linux — este teste confirma que essa não é só uma escolha de CI, é **necessário** para um binário Windows correto.

Fork: [`RicSchonfelder/opencode-i18n-pt`](https://github.com/RicSchonfelder/opencode-i18n-pt) (branch `feat/pt-br-stable`, base `v1.18.25`).

I'd like to work on this.

The report is exact, and the repository already contains the control case for it: the same dialog has a second format that does not have the bug.

**Why the markdown file starts partway in** — the markdown export is built in the TUI from the *loaded* window, while the JSON export is built on the server from storage.

| Step | Location (v2) |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/export` command, both formats | `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:1113` (`id: "session.export"`, `slash: { name: "export" }`) |
| markdown branch — client-side | `:1132` `formatSessionTranscript(sessionData, messages(), options.thinking, options.tools)` |
| JSON branch — server-side | `:1134` `client.api.session.export({ sessionID, sanitize })` |
| what `messages()` is | `:160` `const messages = () => data.session.message.list(route.sessionID)` — the same list the timeline pages into |
| the formatter itself | `:3608` `formatSessionTranscript(session, messages, thinking, tools)` — a pure formatter over the array it is handed; it cannot page |
| server side of the JSON path | `packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:166` → `SessionTransfer.export` → `packages/core/src/session/transfer.ts` reads `sessions.messages({ sessionID, order: "asc" })` |

So the markdown formatter can only ever see the messages the client has currently loaded, and the loaded window is exactly what scrolling changes — which is why step 5 of your repro produces the full file. The JSON format of the same dialog returns the whole session, because `transfer.export` reads the messages from storage with no window at all. Same session, same dialog, different data source: a free A/B check for anyone verifying the fix.

**Two surfaces, not one.** The sibling command at `:1105` (`Copy session transcript`) calls the same `formatSessionTranscript(sessionData, messages(), true)`, so copying from a long thread silently copies the same partial window.

**Fix options**

1. Point the markdown path at the complete history as well — page the rest in (or use the full-items view) before formatting, keeping the formatter where it is.
2. Move the markdown rendering server-side and expose a `format` next to the existing `sanitize` on `session.export`, so both formats are built from `transfer.export`'s complete message list. This removes the second, divergent copy of the transcript logic and makes "complete by construction" true for every format.

My default is (2), because the server-side source is already complete and the endpoint already has the query-parameter shape for it; (1) is the smaller diff if you'd rather not grow the export API. Happy to implement either.

One related question: should an export that cannot see the whole session fail or warn instead of writing a file that looks complete? That is the part of the report that costs users data, and it is independent of which fix above you prefer — I would make the markdown path refuse to write when the client cannot prove it has the full range, unless you'd rather keep it best-effort.

Happy to have the issue assigned if either direction looks right.

Quoting the affected frontmatter values works around it.

The models.dev catalog still stores `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1`, but since #48943 that template is not copied onto the native Workers AI provider. The resolver builds the endpoint from the saved account ID instead. With `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` unset, these all resolve to `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<saved-id>/ai/v1`:

- a Workers AI credential `configuration.accountId`
- `providers.cloudflare-workers-ai.settings.accountId`
- legacy credential `metadata.accountId`

`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is required to resolve the provider endpoint` still happens only if `settings.baseURL` itself still contains the unresolved `${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}` template. Endpoint validation substitutes environment variables only, and it runs before the saved account ID is applied. The current catalog path does not leave that template in settings.
